name: Bifrost security
description: High-precision security policies backed by exact structural identity and value-flow evidence.

policies.severity_rationale: Attacker-controlled data used as JDBC SQL structure can change the executed statement and compromise application data.
policies.remediation: Use a PreparedStatement with placeholders and bind untrusted values through typed setter methods instead of concatenating SQL text.

policies.severity_rationale: Attacker-controlled command text can execute unintended operating-system commands with the application's privileges.
policies.remediation: Avoid passing untrusted text to Runtime.exec. Use a fixed executable and validate arguments against an allowlist.

policies.severity_rationale: A command string built from the process environment or the launch arguments runs in a subshell with the application's privileges, so attacker-controlled text changes the executed command.
policies.remediation: Do not pass process input to os.system. Use subprocess.run with an argument list and shell=False, and validate the executable against an allowlist.

policies.severity_rationale: A request value persisted through the declared store and read back into SQL text can change the executed statement and compromise application data.
policies.remediation: Pass untrusted values through the driver's parameter-binding contract instead of adding them to the SQL text.

policies.severity_rationale: A request value stored without the validator the workspace requires bypasses the application's own reviewed storage invariant.
policies.remediation: Pass request-derived values through the configured validator before storing them, or narrow the reviewed configuration if the obligation does not apply.

policies.severity_rationale: External input written as raw XML text can terminate the intended element or add attacker-controlled XML structure.
policies.remediation: Escape untrusted XML text with SecurityElement.Escape or write it through a typed XmlWriter value API instead of WriteRaw.

policies.severity_rationale: External input embedded in an XPath expression can alter node selection and expose or modify unintended data.
policies.remediation: Use a parameterized XPath mechanism where available, or validate and encode values according to the XPath context before building the expression.

policies.severity_rationale: External input compiled as CodeDom source becomes executable code in the application's process and privileges.
policies.remediation: Do not compile external text. Select a fixed implementation or validate a bounded data representation before processing it.

policies.severity_rationale: External input embedded in a DirectorySearcher LDAP filter can change the directory query and return unintended entries.
policies.remediation: Use a reviewed LDAP filter encoder before interpolation, or construct the query from an allowlisted representation; this public pack does not model third-party encoders.

policies.severity_rationale: External input used as an assembly path can load an unintended local or remote assembly into the process.
policies.remediation: Resolve assemblies from a fixed allowlist and use Path.GetFileName only as a component of validation, not as the sole authorization decision.
